root_cause: The engine's state file is untracked, so on a fresh runner it does not exist and every product was defaulted to the starting price, which reset the whole shop to three dollars every Friday, reverted any price that had been set by hand, and left the engine unable to learn from a run because it started from nothing every time. The hold path also skipped the clamp, so a stored price outside the rule was published and then refused by the command that lists a product for sale, and a product that is held could never move.
evidence: the state file is in .gitignore, the Friday lane runs pricing.py on a fresh checkout, and the catalogue's own price was never read
repro: run pricing.py against a catalogue with a price of five dollars and no state file
fix: the catalogue is the price of record, a hold is clamped like a move is, and the catalogue decides the tier rather than the engine's note
regression_test: audit_selftest.py runs the engine against a catalogue with a price of five dollars and one outside the rule, and checks both
verification: defaulting to the starting price again makes the checks fail

symptom: a corrupt budget crashed the job instead of refusing it
root_cause: The state file's shape was only checked at the top level, so a file holding a months list instead of a table, or a month that was a number instead of a record, or an hour count that was a word, made spent() raise out of check(). The module promises that an unreadable budget refuses the job. The hours and the broken-ness also came from two separate reads of the same file, so a failed read and a successful one could be combined, and the job was approved on zeros from the failed one.
evidence: a state file holding {"months": []} made check() raise an AttributeError, and one holding a non-numeric hour count raised a ValueError
repro: put each of those shapes in data/budget.json and run budget.py check
fix: the shape is checked before it is used, one read answers both questions, and the temporary file has a unique name so two writers cannot swap each other's file into place
regression_test: audit_selftest.py covers the shape of the state file
verification: putting the old check back makes a corrupt file crash again

symptom: the daily lane believed a corrupt budget was a full month
root_cause: The daily lane asked budget.remaining() for the hours left, and remaining() reads a corrupt state as zero spent, so it answered with a whole month while the truth was unknown. The command that answers this question properly, budget.check(), refuses when the hours cannot be read, and the lane did not use it.
evidence: with a corrupt budget file, broken() was true, check() returned 1 and remaining() returned 30.0
repro: corrupt data/budget.json and run the daily lane
fix: the lane asks budget.check(), which refuses when the hours cannot be read
regression_test: the refusal is the answer, not a number
verification: the daily lane asked for a number again

symptom: the daily lane recorded changes that never happened
root_cause: The lane decided whether anything changed by comparing the bytes of the improver's state file before and after. The improver rewrites that file on every path, including the model proposing nothing and the patch being rejected and rolled back, so the bytes always differed and the lane always said a change had been made. It recorded changes that never happened and started the cooldown on days when nothing was done, so the promise that doing nothing is a success never held.
evidence: the improver rewrites its state file on every path, with a fresh timestamp, so the comparison was always true
repro: run the lane and look at whether it says a change was made when the model declined
fix: the lane reads what the improver recorded, and a change means a patch was kept
regression_test: the lane asks for the recorded outcome rather than the file bytes
verification: comparing the bytes again makes every run claim a change

symptom: the daily lane threw away the patch it had tested
root_cause: The lane committed only the four data files, so the improved generator was written into the working tree, tested there and then thrown away with the runner, while the note saying it had been tried was committed. The memory of the attempt survived and the attempt did not, so the same patch was proposed every day and never kept.
evidence: the commit step staged four data files and nothing else, and the patched file was never staged
repro: read the commit step of the daily lane
fix: the patch is staged with the notes, so a patch that passed the suite is kept
regression_test: the lane's own commit step
verification: removing the staging of the changed files leaves the patch on the runner

symptom: the private-data guard was defeated by a shallow checkout
root_cause: The check that looks for a credential which was committed and then deleted reads the whole log, and the runners checked out one commit by default, so in CI it never saw more than the latest commit while it did see the history on a full clone. The lanes that run it were given the whole history. The scan also failed on a full clone over a test fixture that had been removed from the working tree months earlier, so the gate was red for everybody and meaningless.
evidence: the runners use the default shallow checkout, and a full clone found a token-shaped test fixture in the history that is not in the working tree
repro: run check_repo_hygiene.py on a full clone and on a shallow one
fix: the lanes fetch the whole history, and an obvious placeholder is not treated as a leaked secret
regression_test: check_repo_hygiene.py is run by five lanes
verification: the placeholder is still treated as a secret

symptom: the repair lane could never run, because there was nothing to read
root_cause: The repair lane was handed the failure log to diagnose, and it looked for it in a directory that nothing in this repository ever wrote, and for an artifact that no workflow ever uploaded. So it found nothing on every run, said so and gave up before it asked anything, and the repair-after-a-failed-generation capability had never existed.
evidence: there is no selfheal/ directory, nothing writes the two files it looked for, and the only artifacts uploaded are named paid-build and slingshot-installer
repro: run the repair lane and see that it finds no log
fix: the generate job keeps its output as an artifact, the workflow downloads it, and the repair lane looks in the places the log can land
regression_test: the lane's own log handling
verification: removing the new places makes the lane find nothing again

symptom: no build was ever steered by the community's vote
root_cause: The ballot was a weekly thing, opened on Monday and meant to steer the build on Friday, but it was only ever closed once it had aged out after twenty-one days. The Friday step was named 'Close this week's ballot' and ran the Monday job, which opens a ballot and refuses to open a second one. So the same ballot stayed open for three weeks, the build never saw a closed ballot, and the vote steered nothing.
evidence: the ballot lifetime is twenty-one days, the Friday step ran the Monday job, and vote_steer.py reads the winners of closed ballots
repro: run the Friday lane and look at whether the build was steered
fix: the ballot can be closed on demand, and the Friday lane closes it before the build reads the vote
regression_test: the weekly stage the Friday lane must run is checked by the audit
verification: removing the force close leaves the ballot open and the build unsteered

symptom: a corrupted state file took the daily lane down
root_cause: The lane's own state file was only checked at the top level, so a file holding a changes list instead of a table, or a list holding something that was not a record, made the cooldown check raise an AttributeError. A corrupted file took the lane down with a traceback instead of skipping the day, and the write was not atomic, so a crash mid-write left a truncated file that the next read took for an empty history.
evidence: a state file holding {"changes": {"a": 1}} raised an AttributeError in the cooldown check
repro: put each of those shapes in the daily lane's state file
fix: the shape is checked before it is used, and the write goes to a side file and is swapped in
regression_test: the lane's own state handling
verification: the old check crashes again
